discovery: Theoretical prediction and experimental discovery of time-reversal-invariant topological insulators and the quantum spin Hall effect
subfield: Condensed matter physics (topological phases of matter)
motivation: Kane and Mele showed in 2005 that spin-orbit coupling can produce a time-reversal-invariant topological phase, the quantum spin Hall insulator. They identified the Z2 invariant that separates it from ordinary insulators and predicts helical edge states protected by symmetry. Molenkamp's group observed quantized edge conductance in HgTe quantum wells in 2007, confirming a sharp, testable prediction through transport measurements in real devices. This work opened the field of topological insulators and, through the Fu-Kane proposal of proximity-induced superconductivity on topological surfaces, the field of topological superconductivity and Majorana bound states. It unified symmetry, topology and boundary physics in electronic materials, and it now organizes a large part of research on quantum materials, from Weyl semimetals to hybrid superconducting junctions. Few ideas in modern condensed matter physics have combined conceptual depth and experimental impact so clearly.
